newsitem.title: USA: BOXING-BOTHA SCORES KNOCKOUT, NAZAROV, JOPPY RETAIN TITLES.
newsitem.headline: BOXING-BOTHA SCORES KNOCKOUT, NAZAROV, JOPPY RETAIN TITLES.

text.p: South African Francois Botha, looking to climb back to the top of the heavyweight boxing world, scored a 10th-round knockout of James Stanton of Philadelphia Saturday night.

In his first bout since he lost to Michael Moorer in an International Boxing Federation (IBF) heavyweight title fight November 9, 1996, Botha won the vacant World Boxing Association (WBA) North American heavyweight title.

But Botha, who had been stripped of the IBF title he won in December 1995 after testing positive for steroids, has his sights set higher -- maybe on World Boxing Council champion Lennox Lewis of Britain.
"I heard a rumour Lennox Lewis wants to fight me," said Botha. "Let's get it on. I'm ready to fight him."
Botha (36-1, 22 inside the distance) withstood punishing body shots and uppercuts from Stanton in the third and fourth rounds to stage his own late flurry of hard body blows and head punches.
"I took my time, I wanted to work him and get some rounds in," Botha said. "Since the layoff I'm a little rusty."
Stanton (16-3, 8 KOs) was a last-minute replacement for Floridian Lee Gilbert, who dropped out of the card.
A couple of undefeated titleholders were also on the card.
Russian Orzubek Nazarov defended his WBA lightweight title for the sixth time with a seventh-round knockout of top contender Leavander Johnson of Atlantic City, New Jersey.
Nazarov (24-0, 18 KOs) knocked Johnson down twice in the sixth round and put him away for good 17 seconds into the seventh round.
It was only Nazarov's second appearance in the United States. He lives and fights primarily in Japan.
"He is very strong," said the 30-year-old Nazarov. "Some of the blows I hit him with were very hard. He had the will to win. I didn't think I would take him out quickly."

William Joppy (24-0-1, 19 KOs) of Washington, D.C., retained his WBA middleweight belt with a unanimous decision over Peter Venancio (34-2-1, 26 KOs) of Sao Paulo, Brazil. The judges had it 114-112, 114-113 and 115-112.

WBA junior featherweight champion Antonio Cermeno (27-1, 16 KOs) of Venezuela defended his title for the third time with a unanimous 12-round decision over fourth-ranked contender Angel Chacon of Puerto Rico. It was Chacon's first defeat as a pro.

Cermeno opened a cut under Chacon's right eye early and was never in trouble. There was a brief skirmish in the ring after the decision was announced. Chacon's trainer and promoter Tico Zabala had to be restrained.
One of the four scheduled world title fights fell out less than 24 hours before the card started.

IBF junior flyweight champion Mauricio Pastrana of Colombia (16-0, 13 KOs) failed to show for his title defence against IBF fourth-ranked contender Manuel Herrera of the Dominican Republic (18-5-1, 7 KOs).
Pastrana was treated late Friday night in the emergency room of a Miami hospital for severe testicular pain. It was determined that he has epididymitis and will be treated with antibiotics.
The IBF declared the title vacant.
